Here is what I found and fixed:

- **Required checks on the PRs:** the CI runs I dispatched by hand were green, but GitHub does not count them toward a PR's required checks. Only the PR's own `pull_request` runs count, and the originals were wedged. Closing and reopening #474 and #478 gave them fresh runs on the same heads. Their heads, Entire trails, findings (zero) and approvals were all preserved. #472's original run ended in `startup_failure`, so I re-ran it instead.
- **Approvals recorded at exact heads:** #478 at `ce51ee81`, #474 at `2b4c98e4` and #472 at `d199dfae`.
- **Memory:** I saved this as a note so the next incident doesn't cost the same time.

**Where each PR stands, all waiting on their fresh `pull_request` CI runs:**

| PR | Head | State |
|---|---|---|
| #474 | `2b4c98e4` | ACCEPT, zero findings, approved. Waiting on CI. |
| #478 | `ce51ee81` | ACCEPT, zero findings, approved. Waiting on CI. |
| #472 | `d199dfae` | ACCEPT, zero findings, approved. Waiting on CI. |
| #469 | being fixed | The last fix agent has pushed and is waiting on CI. Entire's finding list and the independent review of the new head are still to come. |
| #434, #477 | pushed fixes | Waiting on CI and Entire. Each needs an independent review at its new head. |

One thing I did that I hadn't planned: I enabled auto-merge on #472 before approving it. All its other conditions already hold, so it will merge as soon as its required checks pass. I'm treating that as acceptable and will verify the merge happened at the right head. I'll merge #474 and #478 as their checks go green, and I'll watch whether Entire's "Up to date" gate blocks the later ones once the first lands.

No defect rises above Low.

**Consumers of the old prefix.**
- `rg '\[Nexus'` over `cli/src` finds no remaining recogniser. Every hit is a producer string or a tool-result decoration.
- The four prefix-based consumers are gone: compaction's earlier task requests (`agent.ts:3333`), the current request (`:3612`), the findings request (`:3744`), and the TUI objective (`tui.ts:95`).

**Producers.**
- Against `v1.1.3`, every user-role push of a Nexus note is now created through `harnessNoteMessage`: recovery (`:6423`), cut-off (`:6600`, `:7590`), parser notices (`:6718`), empty reply (`:6736`), continuation (`:6749`) and subagent recovery (`:7684`).

**Can an operator, model or tool string acquire provenance?**
- Only through the legacy migration on load. It is not called on any live path, and `setMessages` has no callers in `src`.
- Provider output and tool results never pass through `harnessNoteMessage` as message role. The sidecar protocol does not construct `ChatMessage`s.
- A hand-edited session file can set `harness` directly. That is the same trust level as the existing `"skill-note"` marker and needs local write access. It is not a new boundary.
- The marker carries no authority. A note is still a user-role message to the model, and `harness` only classifies it for compaction, the findings request and the history view.

**Legacy migration.**
- It never demotes or rewrites content. It skips any message where `harness !== undefined`, returns a new array and replaces the element with `{...message, harness:"note"}`. That makes it idempotent and non-mutating.
- It is anchored on the exact wording of each v1.1.3 note. The regexes match the real v1.1.3 producer strings and the parser notice strings.
- It also requires a position: not the first message, and after an assistant message, a tool message, a marked note or a non-first system message. Only the cut-off note may follow an unmarked user message.
- The accepted ambiguity is a v1.1.3 operator message that pastes a legacy note verbatim after a reply. I judge the tradeoff sound. The pasted text is the operator's own, in an already-saved session, and the consequence is only that the message is left out of the "Earlier task requests" list and out of the findings request. The text is still sent to the model unchanged, and nothing is hidden from the operator or gains authority.
- The FINDINGS claim that new messages are never affected holds, since migration runs on load only.

**`keptNotes` and `compactionCandidate`.**
- A trailing run of unanswered harness notes after the operator request is kept whole.
- The real operator request is now always kept verbatim as `currentUserIndex`. At base, a trailing recovery note was treated as the current user message and the real request was summarised away, so this is an improvement.
- Candidate filters and the final `selected.set` are consistent, and the order is preserved by sorting on index.

### Suggestions (all Low)

1. **Low — `cli/src/agent.ts:3617` (the author's item 1: queued steering after an unanswered note drops the note).**
   - **Trigger:** `endStep` pushes a recovery or cut-off note, then `applyQueuedSteering` pushes steering before the next request, and compaction runs on that request.
   - **Effect:** The steering message is an unmarked user message, so it becomes `currentUserIndex` and the earlier note falls outside `keptNotes`. That note is a one-shot retry hint and gets summarised away. This is the same behaviour as base, not a regression.
   - **Loss or leak:** No operator intent is lost, because the steering message is kept and the objective is pinned. Nothing leaks.
   - **Fix:** In the loop at `:3617`, keep marked notes after the last operator request even when later unmarked user messages are steering, for example by skipping `pinnedUserText(...)` messages when walking back. Alternatively, record the limitation in FINDINGS.

2. **Low — `cli/src/harness_notes.ts:49-50` (the author's item 2: migration is not exact for compacted v1.1.3 sessions).**
   - **Trigger:** A v1.1.3 post-compaction session where a retained note sits directly after an unmarked user message, other than a cut-off note. That is a shape v1.1.3 compaction should not normally produce, since its last user message was the note itself.
   - **Effect:** The note stays unmarked and is treated as operator text, which only affects compaction's earlier-task list, the findings request and the TUI objective. Because it is user-role text either way, nothing is hidden from or leaked to the model beyond what v1.1.3 already did.
   - **Fix:** None required. The conservative choice is deliberate, because widening it would promote real operator messages.

3. **Low — `cli/test/context_convergence.test.ts:1681` (the CTX-06 `doesNotMatch` can never fail).**
   - **Trigger:** `priorTasks` is rendered as one joined line, and the first entry in the fixture is "Review the cache layer". The regex is anchored on `Earlier task requests: \[Nexus ...`, so a leaked note in any later position still passes. That makes the negative assertion for continuation, recovery and empty-reply notes vacuous. The old assertion had the same weakness, and the rewrite did not strengthen it.
   - **Coverage elsewhere:** The new positive assertion (the prefixed operator text is listed) would fail under a prefix-based recogniser and does protect the intended property. `harness_provenance.test.ts` also covers the empty-reply note with `[\s\S]*`.
   - **Fix:** Use `assert.doesNotMatch(content, /Earlier task requests[^\n]*\[Nexus (?:continuation|recovery)|\[Nexus: your reply was empty/)`.

4. **Low (docs) — `docs/v1.1.4/FINDINGS.md:108`.** The row is marked FIXED but does not record the two residual limitations in items 1 and 2. Add one sentence naming them so the row stays truthful to its limits. Everything else in the row matches the code and tests.

## Tests
- `harness_provenance.test.ts` would fail with a prefix-based recogniser:
  - The `SPOOF` request is expected in "Earlier task requests", as the current request, and as the findings "Current request".
  - The marked note is expected to be excluded, and unanswered notes are expected to survive compaction.
  - The migration tests check idempotency, no mutation, never-first, and that `"[Nexus] hello"`, a note contained in other text, and a malformed counter are not migrated.
  - A table of the real v1.1.3 wordings is migrated.
- The test is not red-verified against base, since it imports a module that is absent there. It is nonetheless behavioural.

## Slop rating: **Low**
- The strongest positives are that there is a single recogniser with no duplicated logic, producers collapse into one helper, and the migration is anchored on the real wording and covered by a per-note-kind test.
- The only slop is the vacuous negative regex in CTX-06 and a long migration doc comment that restates the rule. There is no dead code, no stale references, and `SKILL_NOTE_PREFIX` was cleanly removed from `agent.ts`.

### Good
- Marker-only trust and conservative, position-aware migration with an explicit, documented tradeoff.
- Operator requests are now retained verbatim in compaction even with trailing notes.
- The sidecar history and the TUI share the same recogniser, which closes the earlier PR #467 Low row.

I stopped before reading the end of `line_rows`, `markdown.rs` and `live.rs` in full, because you asked for the report now. Repo rule used from the base: root `AGENTS.md` ("keep existing comments"). I found no violation of it.

## 1. Code review

**C1. A notice replaces the approve-all question while the confirm is still armed. Medium, confidence 0.8.**
- Location: `live_view.rs:661-669` (`match approval.notice { Some(..) => notice, None if confirming => confirm_hint }`), with `live_state.rs:1526-1539` and `1555-1558`.
- Trigger at 80x24, empty draft:
  1. `a` asks the question and `confirming` becomes true.
  2. `a` again within 1 s sets `APPROVAL_CONFIRM_JUST_OPENED` and keeps `confirming`.
  3. The hint row now holds only the notice. Below about 81 columns it shows the head "ignored: confirm question just opened", without the "press again to approve all later actions" tail. The question and "(switches to auto)" are not on screen.
  4. After 1 s of quiet, `a` or Enter calls `decide(ApprovedForSession)` and switches the session to auto.
- The same happens through the guard path. A scroll-key burst re-arms the guard without clearing `confirming`, so `a` → ignored notice → quiet → `a` confirms.
- The sweep's `read_through` presses `a` and Enter 3 s apart, so it never hits this. `check_answerable_frame` requires the question only when `notice` is `None`.
- Fix: clear `confirming` when a notice is raised, or reserve a row so the question stays drawn.

**C2. `note_approval_shown` discards a longer guard. Low, confidence 0.5.**
- Location: `live_state.rs:1321-1326`. On a `shown` false→true flip it assigns `guard_until = in_flight.then(..)`.
- `bulk_input_at` (a paste) calls `rearm_guard` but does not set `last_key`. If the pasted draft makes the panel un-fit for a frame, and it re-fits more than 1 s after the last typed key, `guard_until` resets to `None`. The 1 s held-key window from the paste is lost.

**C3. A screen below 40x10 shows no hint that an approval is pending. Low, confidence 0.8.**
- Location: `live_view.rs:112-122`. `render_live` returns `LiveLayout::default()` with only "Nexus needs a larger terminal".
- Esc still denies, silently. Invariant (c) is true only for panel-level rendering.
- The sweep skips this case because it looks for ╭ and ╰ rows before demanding "enlarge".

**C4. A draft of up to 6 composer rows un-fits the panel, and the message blames the terminal. Low.**
- The sweep tests only a 3-line draft. Backspace and Esc still recover, so this is an availability issue only.

## 2. Security review

**S1. The panel can show less than the patch applies. High, confidence 0.9. Not introduced by this diff.**
- The code was already like this at base, so it is out of scope for the "introduced by this change" rule. It is the largest unswept state for the claim "y approves only after every row was on screen".
- Display path: `live_state.rs:966` parses the joined review rows with `diff_view::parse`. `live_view.rs:672-679` then draws only the parsed patch rows. `parse` reads hunk bodies by their `@@` counts (`diff_view.rs:163-195`). A ±/space line after the declared counts falls to the final `else if` branch (`diff_view.rs:240`) and is silently dropped. `@@ ` lines whose header does not parse are also dropped, and `@@` without a trailing space is not treated as a header.
- Apply path: `core/src/file_ops.rs:1206+` ignores counts. Everything after the first `@@` is hunk content, `---` and `+++` are skipped only before the first hunk, and all hunks are applied to `args.path`.
- Request that triggers it (cli/src/approval_review.ts passes the patch through unchanged):
  ```json
  {"type":"approval.request","id":"a1","turn_id":"t1","tool":"patch_file","subject":"cfg.toml","preview":"",
   "review":{"kind":"patch","path":"cfg.toml","truncated":false,
   "patch":"--- a/cfg.toml\n+++ b/cfg.toml\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-debug = true\n+debug = false\n-sandbox = true\n+sandbox = false\n"}}
  ```
- At any size, the panel shows only `-debug = true` / `+debug = false`. Every key (PageDown until `read_all`, then `y`) approves. The applier then replaces both `debug = true` and `sandbox = true`, provided they are consecutive in the file.
- Fix: when the parsed hunk lines are fewer than the review's ±/space rows, or any non-blank row was dropped, fall back to drawing `approval.lines`. Add a sweep kind with mismatched counts.

**S2. Multi-file patch. Low.**
- File heading rows are filtered out (`live_view.rs:677`) and "Proposed:" counts only `files.first()`. The applier writes every hunk to `args.path` regardless of headers. All hunk rows are drawn, but the file boundaries and counts are misleading.

**S3. Invisible-character gaps. Low.**
- Not mapped by `approval_visible_control`: U+FFFC, the Arabic format characters (U+0600-0605, 06DD, 070F, 08E2), and combining or enclosing marks such as U+0338 and U+20DD. They are not caught by the sweep either.
- The sweep's `forbidden()` is the same list as the production predicate, so it cannot find a character both omit.
- A literal `<U+200B>` in a command looks identical to its stand-in.

No new injection or path-traversal route was found in the diff. Control, bidi and tag characters are neutralised at the single `review_lines` choke point, and `\n` becomes ␊ before the join, so a fake diff header cannot be injected through `before`, `after` or `path`.

## 3. Slop: Medium

- **Overbuilt timing machinery.** Five overlapping timers (`APPROVAL_GUARD`, `TYPING_RUN`, `REPEAT_QUIET`, `CONFIRM_DELAY`, `IN_FLIGHT`) plus `last_key`, `last_text`, `confirm_asked_at` and `rearm_guard`, grown over many fix rounds. They interact in ways the sweep does not exercise, and C1 and C2 come from that interaction.
- **Sweep proves less than it claims.** "Whole state space" is defined by the display model and mirrors the production predicate, so S1 and S3 are invisible to it. The reader is the same code that drops rows. The doc comment and the manual claim more than the tests establish.
- **Debris:** `let _ = state;` with an unused `state` parameter in `check_answerable_frame`, and the odd `(0x1bu32..=0x1b)` range in `bad()`. Smaller points: `scan_every_page` swaps the subject for "x", and drafts and queue are crossed only partially.

## Sweep gaps checked

States I traced and found safe:
- **Queued approval promoted after an answer:** `promote_pending_approval` resets `shown=false`, and `read_all`/`seen_through` start fresh. The next draw resets `seen_width`. `y`/Enter/`n`/`a` set `last_key`, so the guard arms. Esc leaves `last_key` unset, but a held Esc only denies.
- **Resize between frames:** the stale `read_all` reflects a full read at the old width. The next frame resets it on a width change, and a too-small screen resets it via `LiveLayout::default()`.
- **Notice longer than the reserved rows:** the heads are 37 columns at most, and Screen mode has an inner width of at least 38. Truncation is reachable only when `render_approval` is called alone below about 31 columns.
- **Layout flapping from notices or the question:** `fits` depends on `hint_rows`, which takes the maximum of the default and confirm hints. A notice or the question never changes `fits`, `gaps` or `viewport`.
- **CJK, emoji, long single words:** `markdown::wrap`, `wrap_at_breaks` and `fit_rows` all measure by grapheme width and never split a wide character. Only widths of 1 overflow. Long space runs overshoot by one trailing space. The sweep has no wide-character content, so this is untested but looks correct.
- **Empty subject or tool:** the heading is always at least one row. An empty `run_command` leaves no body rows, `shown` is true, and the panel states what it is.
- **Huge subject:** the sidecar caps it at 200 characters. Each invisible character expands about 8x as `<U+XXXX>`, so about 200 of them (a few dozen heading rows) refuse at 80x24 — Deny only. That is an availability limit, not a safety one.
- **Burst containing an answer:** a burst stops at its first action, and decision keys are inert after `rearm_guard` and `last_text`.

Minor, not in the sweep: in the patch branch, "Proposed: change c.txt" strips a leading `b/` from a real path `b/c.txt` (`diff_view.rs:224`). The heading shows the true path from `subject`.</result>

<result>### Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES at c3b260fdcebb72394a1a01503dfaaf384d494d5d

- The head matches `origin/v1/v114-wp1316-auto-inputs`. The diff base is `29e7ebff9a6f171438115d8a404a5f18a3fe4bc1`.
- I read the code only (git, rg, reading files). Nothing was built or run.
- The review rules (REVIEW.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) were not found at the base, and no finding rests on one.

### Blockers

**1. Security, Medium (high confidence): host-side git runs in a model-writable worktree with no checkout trust boundary**
- Where: `cli/src/core/specialist_inputs.ts:274-284` (`git()`, `cwd: root`) and `attributesTree` at :233. Also `cli/src/core/operation_git.ts:434-449` (`snapshotCandidate`'s `run`, `cwd: entry.worktree`).
- On main, `cli/src/git.ts:38` `trustedGitArgs` calls `verifyCheckout` (`cli/src/core/checkout_trust.ts:106`) and pins `--git-dir/--work-tree`. Its header says host-side git must not run where the sandboxed agent could have planted `.git` or a nested repo.
- The new code never calls either one. Neither `trustedGitArgs` nor `verifyCheckout` appears anywhere in `specialist_inputs.ts` or in the new `operation_git.ts` code.
- Trigger: the model, which owns the unit worktree, replaces the worktree's `.git` pointer with a directory, or points it at another gitdir.
  - The diff and the snapshot are then built from the attacker's repository: its index, HEAD and object alternates.
  - `GIT_SAFE` is a denylist of known config keys. `trace2.eventTarget` and `trace2.perfTarget` (append to a path) and `remote.*.uploadpack` with a lazy fetch (on git before 2.44, where `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` is ignored) are not in it.
  - On the snapshot path, `fs.copyFileSync` copies a file whose path comes from `rev-parse --git-path index` in that planted repo.
- Fix: call `verifyCheckout(workspace)` first in both builders and refuse on a reason, as `trustedGitArgs` does. Prepend the returned `--git-dir/--work-tree` pair to every `git` call here, including `attributesTree`. Add red-first tests for a replaced `.git` file and a nested `.git` directory.

**2. Behaviour change for `reviewer` and `acceptance_reviewer`, and a false doc claim**
- Where: `cli/src/core/operation_runner_execution.ts:728-741` (`reviewEvidence`), against `docs/v1.1.4/FINDINGS.md` A4.
- On main, `reviewCandidateDiff` produced a diff for any repository state. Now `candidateDiff` refuses any of these:
  - an LFS or git-crypt `filter=` attribute
  - a submodule
  - `core.filemode=false` (common on WSL/NTFS mounts)
  - a subdirectory workspace
  - any sparse or assume-unchanged entry
- That refusal becomes `diffError`, and `operation_runner_execution.ts:392` blocks the review unit with an operator question.
- FINDINGS says "the specialist runs without the auto-collected diff and is told why; the operation is not broken". That is true only for `security_reviewer`. Reviewers hard-block.
- Fix, either:
  - for reviewer roles, fall back to the previous simple diff, applying the protected-path filter, when the predicate refuses; or
  - state in FINDINGS and the PR description that reviewers now block on these states, and get that accepted explicitly.
- The `core.ignorecase=true` refusal also hits macOS and Windows default repos, though v1 is Linux-only per DEC-12.

### Suggestions

- `specialist_inputs.ts:99-101`: the `--show-object-format` handling is wrong in three ways.
  - **What is true:** the option belongs to the SHA-256 work of roughly git 2.28/2.29, not 2.38. The installed 2.43 man page lists `--show-object-format[=(storage|input|output)]` with no version. I could not confirm the exact release offline. Older git cannot open a SHA-256 repository anyway.
  - **The catch is wrong:** it swallows every failure (timeout, permissions, corruption) and assumes sha1. Rev-parse also usually echoes unknown flags with exit 0, so on old git the `format !== "sha1"` branch would refuse every repository with a nonsense reason. I could not verify the echo behaviour locally.
  - Fix: delete the comment's version claim. Treat only a clean "unknown option" as sha1, and let other errors propagate.
- `specialist_inputs.ts:226`: `attributesTree` silently drops a `.gitattributes` over 1 MiB or unreadable. The predicate (:125) reads files of any size and only checks for `filter=`, so the stripped attribute tree can lack `text`/`eol` rules the tester's own commit applies. The snapshot then differs silently, which is the failure the predicate exists to prevent. Fix: refuse in the predicate when a `.gitattributes` is over the limit or unreadable.
- `specialist_inputs.ts:295` and `operation_git.ts:~460`: `execFileSync(..., encoding: "utf8")` decodes non-UTF-8 path bytes lossily.
  - Paths round-tripped as pathspecs then mismatch. `candidateDiff` fails with a raw git message, which fails closed but is outside the predicate.
  - `check-attr --stdin` receives mangled names, so a rule in `$GIT_DIR/info/attributes` that matches only the real bytes can be missed.
  - Fix: refuse in `snapshotSupport` when any listed path contains U+FFFD. Add a test.
- `operation_git.ts:~466`: the snapshot's `ownIndex` path goes through `.trim()` plus `existsSync`, then falls back to `read-tree HEAD`. A mismatched path silently drops the unit's staged state. Fall back only on ENOENT.
- `operation_git.ts:204-235`: a stale-snapshot restart deletes the old worktree and branch before `snapshotCandidate` can throw. A refusal then leaves a record pointing at removed state. A retry self-heals, so this is low. Build the snapshot first.
- Snapshot scope: `add -A` excludes ignored files (`node_modules`, build output, `.env`). The debugger therefore reproduces on a tree lacking them. This is not recorded as a limitation.
- **Test: `cli/test/specialist_inputs_domain.test.ts` sweep.** It accepts any error matching `git could not produce`, so an in-domain state that regresses to a raw git failure still passes. Require that error only for the states known to produce it.
- **Test: sweep coverage and refusal coverage.**
  - The sweep never calls `snapshotCandidate`.
  - The snapshot-refusal loop (`.filter(!/submodule|merge|core\./)`) skips submodule, merge, filemode, symlinks and ignorecase.
  - Subdirectory and SHA-256 are not tested at the snapshot level.
  - The SHA-256 test returns silently when git lacks support.
- **Docs: `docs/v1.1.4/FINDINGS.md` A4.**
  - It claims "git older than 2.40 ... fails closed with a raw git message". Older git ignores `GIT_ATTR_SOURCE` silently. Only the snapshot's `--path-format=absolute` (2.31) errors.
  - It keeps a stale "(superseded by the supported-domain predicate below ...)" parenthetical mid-cell.
  - It contains the claim "A finding can now only be about the predicate or the domain". Delete that.
  - The cell is about 6 KB, and it is marked FIXED while carrying an OPEN item.
  - Split the row, leaving A4 FIXED and the limitation as its own OPEN row.

- **(1) States outside the predicate:** I found none that silently produce a wrong snapshot or leak files, apart from the gaps above.
  - Symlinks are handled by `lstat` plus `isFile`, git stores the link target without following it, and git rejects paths beyond a symlink.
  - Intent-to-add and detached HEAD are fine; the sweep covers both, and linked worktrees are exercised by the snapshot tests.
  - Merge and cherry-pick states are refused while unresolved. Untracked nested repositories are skipped and counted.
  - Huge files hit timeout and buffer limits and fail closed.
- **(2) The `.trim()` High:** gone. `ls-files`, `ls-files -v`, `ls-files -s`, `check-attr` and `diff --name-status` are all NUL-split and untrimmed. In the snapshot, `raw: true` covers the listings; the remaining trims are scalar.
- **(3) Compaction:** `agent.ts` (about :7221-7236) detects removed, un-re-read observations and returns `UNVERIFIED` / `CONTEXT_EVIDENCE_NOT_RETAINED` for a diagnostic run. A re-read clears the key (:5655). This is detection, not preservation, and it is tested in `context_convergence`. Acceptable.
- **(4) Trust boundary:** blocker 1.
- **(5) Tests:** see the test suggestions above. The refused states have red-first tests for `candidateDiff`.
- **(6) FINDINGS:** the accepted limitation is recorded honestly and in detail, but the problems above remain: the reviewer claim, the git-version claim, and the cell structure.

- The finite-domain predicate replaces per-state patching. A refusal carries an actionable reason.
- The same builder is used for both reviewers and the debugger snapshot. The pinned git environment and stripped attribute tree are well reasoned.
- The snapshot is built in a private index copy and the old record survives a failed `worktree add`.
- `diagnosticRun` is plumbed end to end, and stale snapshots are bound to the failed run.

### Slop: Medium

1. The central assumption is that `GIT_SAFE`, a config denylist, is an adequate trust boundary. It bypasses the repo's established `verifyCheckout`/`trustedGitArgs` mechanism, and FINDINGS and the code comments over-assert completeness.
2. Weak checks for important behaviour: the sweep's escape-hatch error regex, and the snapshot refusal coverage gap. There is also a bloated A4 cell with leftover superseded text, and about 1,100 lines of tests for a heuristic-heavy protected-content comparison.

<result>Review of `00b9cd4a..bfb87a52` in `/home/mike/nexus-wt/v114-int-2`. This was a read-only review of the code. I did not run any tests or the redactor, so every trace below comes from reading it and no timing is measured. The review rules at the diff base are `AGENTS.md` only (`git show 00b9cd4a:AGENTS.md`). There is no `REVIEW.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repo at that commit.

## (a) Can the new logic un-redact something the old code redacted?

The original match is never dropped.
- **scanBase64Keys:** `runEnd` is in the `Set` and skips the charge because `end > runEnd` is false (egress.ts:606).
- **Pattern loop:** `ends = [end]` is pushed unconditionally; only the extended end depends on the charge (egress.ts:1144-1145).
- **`continue` on a failed charge:** it skips only the longer end, so `runEnd` stays redacted. This path cannot remove an original match.

Two narrow paths still lose coverage the old code gave.

1. **Medium (confidence 0.75), egress.ts:606 and :1145. Extensions are now all-or-nothing, and the encoded and dotted ends are charged twice.**
   - **Old behaviour:** the scan was capped at `min(MAX_EXTENSION, budget.left)`. Once less than 1024 remained, the old code still redacted a truncated prefix of the extension. It also charged the encoded and dotted parts once each, as increments.
   - **New behaviour:** the scan runs to the full 1024 and is dropped entirely when `to-from > left`. When both the encoded end and the dotted end are accepted, they are charged `enc-run` plus `ext-run`, which counts the encoded part twice.
   - **Trigger:** one line repeated about 30 times or more: `"sk-ab%2F" + 40 alphanumerics with a digit + "." + 40 key-material chars + " "`.
     - Each block is 90 characters.
     - The new code charges 43 + 84 = 127 per block. The old code charged 43 + 41 = 84.
     - The budget `n + 1024` runs out around block 26-30.
     - Every later block keeps only its `sk-ab` prefix redacted. `%2F<body>.<tail>` stays visible, apart from any entropy-classifier catch, which I did not trace.
     - The old code redacted all of them.
   - **Fix:** either charge only the increment past the highest end already charged for that match, or raise the budget to roughly `2*text.length + MAX_EXTENSION`. Keep the all-or-nothing behaviour only if the loss in the near-exhausted case is accepted.

2. **Low (confidence 0.8), egress.ts:586 and :598-602. A decoy blob adjacent to a real key still withholds that key's extension.** The comment says a crafted prefix "never withholds the extension of a real key that comes after it". That is false once the rescan ceiling is spent.
   - **Trigger:** `"sk-%2F-".repeat(200) + "sk-Qx7Km2Vb9%2FLrTz…"` with no space between them.
     - The blob exhausts `rescanLeft` after about 22 rescans (16n / ~1040 per rescan).
     - The real key's `at` falls inside the last non-rescan decoy's `scannedTo`. It is therefore a rescan with `rescanLeft <= 0`, so `mayExtend` is false.
     - Its run is only `Qx7Km2Vb9`, which is under 20 characters and rejected. The `sk-` pattern also needs at least 20 characters, so deterministic redaction misses the whole key.
   - **Not a regression:** the old code had the same hole and drained its budget faster.
   - **Why it passes the new test:** the new test puts `" then "` between the blob and the key, so the key is a non-rescan.
   - **Fix:** reword the comment and docblock, or cache the contiguous encoded-run end so a rescan does not rescan.

## (b) Quadratic or worse time or output size?

**No quadratic path.** There is one linear amplification with a large constant.

- **scanBase64Keys:** linear.
  - Fresh scans total at most the text, because a non-rescan match starts at or past `scannedTo`.
  - A rejected dotted tail is not counted in `scannedTo`. It contains no encoded units, because normalising units yields `/` or `+`, which always makes a segment key material. So any `sk-` inside the tail is covered by that match's own run, and tails are disjoint.
  - Rescans are capped at 16n by `rescanLeft`.
  - The cost of `isBase64KeyRun` on each of the three ends is covered by the `extendedEnd - runEnd` term, which is charged.
  - Worst case is about 16-50 character-operations per input character.

- **Medium (confidence 0.8), egress.ts:1144 (`extendDottedKey` in the pattern loop). No work ceiling.**
  - **Old behaviour:** `limit = end + min(MAX, budget.left)`, so once the budget was spent the loop did not run. Total work was about n + 1024.
  - **New behaviour:** every regex match whose end is immediately followed by `.` scans up to 1024 characters of segments (slice, `normalizeKeyChars`, regex tests), even after the budget is gone.
  - **Why it is linear:** matches within one pattern are disjoint, so there are at most n / (minimum match length) of them.
  - **Trigger:** a stream of tokens that each match a pattern and are joined by dots. Segments need a digit to count as key material.
    - Example: `xoxb-0123456789.` repeated. SLACK matches at 15+ characters, so there are about n/16 matches, each scanning ~1024 characters (about 64 segments).
    - That is roughly 64x amplification versus the old code. The 7 dotted patterns can stack on the same text, for example `sk-ant-…` matches both the ANTHROPIC and OPENAI patterns.
    - Output size stays bounded, because `ends.push` is guarded by `chargeExtension`.
  - **Fix:** share the `rescanLeft`-style ceiling with the pattern loop, or cache the "continuation end" per dotted run so each dotted run is scanned once. For example, record `scannedTo`/`lastExt` and reuse it when the next match starts inside it.
  - **Test gap:** the new test's `"sk-a.".repeat(20000)` yields 4-character segments that are rejected at once, so it does not exercise this path.

- **Output size:** each emitted value's extension is charged, so values total at most about 3n + budget, as before. I did not find a regression. `resolveOverlaps`' `open` list is unchanged.

## Slop review: Low

The two strongest reasons are the stale comments and the vacuous assertions.

- **Stale comments (low), egress.ts:536 and :577.** `extendDottedKey` has no budget parameter any more, yet line 536 still says "or the budget is spent". Line 577 still says "The longer runs are charged to the extension budget, so the cost is linear". That is now false: linearity comes from the rescan ceiling plus the 1024 caps, and charging only bounds what is kept. This conflicts with the rule at `AGENTS.md:9` ("Maintain documentation integrity…").
- **Unexplained constant (low), egress.ts:586 and :602.** `16` appears twice: `16 * text.length` and `16 +` per rescan. There is no named constant and no explanation.
- **Vacuous assertions (low), live_view.rs:2078-2080.** `lines.len() <= 10` and `chars().count() <= 40` cannot fail, because `TestBackend` always renders exactly width x height cells. Only the `assert_shows` and `╰` checks carry weight.
- **Weak new test (low), `redactor_encoded_dotted.test.ts`.**
  - It has a 5-second wall-clock assertion.
  - It does not cover the adjacent-key case (finding a.2) or the accepted-charge exhaustion case (finding a.1).
  - It does not cover the pattern-loop amplification.
- **README and Rust test edits are fine.** The README flags (`--worktree`, `--worktree-branch`) match `cli/src/index.ts:349-350`. The Rust height test now asserts the real behaviour, a hard-coded 11. The old formula used `rows().len()` while the code uses `unfiltered_len()`.

## Code Review summary

There are no high-severity defects. The findings are the pattern-loop ceiling (medium), the all-or-nothing and double-charge budget (medium), and the adjacent-decoy hole and false comment (low).

## Security Review

There is no new vulnerability. One availability concern applies:
- **Availability:** the pattern-loop CPU amplification above, reachable through untrusted tool output.
- **Disclosure:** the budget-drain cases above only leave the tail of a URL-encoded key visible. That is the same class of hole the old code had, and for the adjacent-decoy case it is easier to reach in the old code.

input.message:
#434 at 00ea64be: Entire found 2 NEW findings the independent reviews missed; severity went UP (1 Low -> 1 High + 1 Medium). Method change: FAIL CLOSED everywhere in the protected-content comparison; stop patching cases. Findings (full text via `entire trail finding list --repo gh/mikeholownych/nexus-code --branch v1/v114-wp1316-auto-inputs --json`): (HIGH 01M76FGWD3VF, specialist_inputs.ts:200-201) if an ignored `.env` is a SYMLINK and its dereferenced contents are copied into a new `notes.txt`, the protected-source check silently skips it because `lstat().isFile()` is false, so the copy reaches the automatic security-review inputs (operation_runner_execution.ts:698-701) including content credential redaction does not recognise. (MEDIUM 01M76FGWDQBF, specialist_inputs.ts:447) with core.filemode=false, reviews use the plainCandidateDiff fallback (operation_runner_execution.ts:732-733) but loading only the BASE index loses staged removals such as `git rm --cached generated.txt` when the ignored file remains unchanged on disk; the index-to-worktree diff then shows no deletion, reviewers get an incomplete candidate or reject its only change as empty; main's `git diff base` preserved that deletion.
DESIGN for this round: (1) Define the comparison's SOUND DOMAIN explicitly: protected sources that are regular files <= a size bound and readable. For EVERY protected path outside that domain (symlink: do not dereference blindly; special file; over the bound; unreadable; changed type) the result is 'cannot compare' and MUST be treated exactly like 'a protected path changed': every new/untracked/added file is OMITTED from the auto-collected inputs (the existing conservative rule), with an explicit note to the reviewer. Never `continue`/skip silently on a protected source. Write a table-driven test over protected-source kinds (regular, symlink to file, symlink to dir, dangling symlink, FIFO if portable, oversized, unreadable via chmod when not root, replaced by a directory, hardlink) x copy shapes (identical content copy, partial copy, dereferenced symlink contents copied into notes.txt) asserting: copied protected content never appears in the output; red-first for the symlink case. Look for OTHER places in specialist_inputs.ts / operation_git.ts that skip non-regular files with lstat().isFile() and apply the same rule (rg 'isFile\(\)|lstat'). (2) For the plainCandidateDiff fallback preserve REAL-INDEX removals: build the scratch index from the base tree, then for every path in the base tree that is ABSENT from the real index (staged removals: `git diff-index --cached --name-status -z <base>` D entries, NUL-split) do `update-index --force-remove` on the scratch index (so `git rm --cached` of a still-present ignored file shows as a deletion), while still not trusting assume-unchanged/skip-worktree flags to hide worktree changes. The repo rules at 29e7ebff are `AGENTS.md` only (no REVIEW.md or CLAUDE.md), and nothing in it bears on these findings. `cli/src/core/specialist_inputs.ts` does not exist at 29e7ebff, so the whole file counts as introduced by the PR, not only the delta.

**F1 (Security, medium, confidence 0.9) — the new symlink rule lets a dereferenced directory symlink through in the plain diff.**
- **Where:** `specialist_inputs.ts:237` (`if (!st.isFile()) return !st.isSymbolicLink();`) together with `:497` (`git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <file>` with `okExit [1]`).

  - `dlnk` is a symlink to `d`, so `carriedBy` returns false for it.
  - `git diff --no-index /dev/null dlnk` then follows the link and prints `+++ b/dlnk/null` with the secret.
- **Verified:** git 2.43 emitted the full content. A symlink to a regular file and a dangling symlink render as link text, which is fine.
- **Regression:** before the delta every non-regular new file was omitted. The main `candidateDiff` is not affected, because it stores the link as a link via intent-to-add.
- **Side effect:** a directory symlink without a file named `null` yields an empty diff that is not counted in `omittedNew`, so the new path vanishes silently.
- **Fix:** return true (carried) for any symlink whose `fs.statSync` target is not a regular file or fails to stat. Alternatively, keep `return true` for all non-regular files in the plain builder.
- **Docs:** the comment at `:236` ("never as content") and the "never dereferenced" claim in `FINDINGS.md` are false for this case.

**F2 (Code, medium, confidence 0.9) — staged-removal handling is wrong in a subdirectory workspace.**
- **Where:** `:468-471`.
- **Trigger:** the workspace is a subdirectory of the repo, which the predicate refuses and the plain builder therefore serves. The existing test at `:222` covers this case but has no staged removal.
- **Mismatch:** `diff-index --cached --name-status` prints root-relative paths, while `update-index --stdin` treats them as relative to the working directory. I reproduced this: from `sub/`, root-level `a/b` removed `sub/a/b` from the private index.
- **Effect:** either the removal is silently not applied (the original bug stays), or a different unchanged file is shown as deleted and also as a new file.
- **Fix:** add `--relative` to the `diff-index` call, which gives cwd-relative paths and matches `git diff --relative` elsewhere. Add a subdirectory test with a staged removal.

**F3 (Security, medium, confidence 0.85) — the plain builder does not treat unchanged tracked protected files as comparison sources.**
- **Where:** `:485` passes `known = [...tracked, ...untracked]`, where `tracked` is only the changed paths (`diff --name-only`). The ignored listing never contains tracked files either.
- **Contrast:** the main builder passes `[...atBase, ...ownIndex, ...untracked]` at `:389`.
- **Trigger:** a plain-served state with `policyWorkspace === root`, so there is no operator listing. A committed, unchanged protected file such as `.env.production` or `secrets.json` is copied to an untracked `notes.txt`, which is then shown. In isolated worktrees the operator listing (`--cached`) covers this.
- **Fix:** pass `[...listed, ...tracked, ...untracked]`. `listed` is already computed at `:474`.

**F4 (Security, low, confidence 0.7) — protected sources with non-UTF-8 names are silently skipped.**
- **Where:** `:215`. A path decoded to U+FFFD gives ENOENT on lstat, which hits the silent `continue` with `complete` still true.
- **Gap:** the predicate's U+FFFD check covers only cached and other files. The plain builder checks only changed and untracked paths. The ignored listing (`:418`) and the operator listing (`:429-431`) are unchecked.
- **Trigger:** an ignored or operator-side protected file with an invalid-UTF-8 name, for example `.env.bak\xff`.
- **Fix:** set `complete = false` when a source path contains U+FFFD.

**F5 (low, informational) — `.nexus` precedence and other residuals.**
- Any path with a `.nexus` segment is compared by exact hash only. Symlinks and files over 4 MiB are skipped silently (`:207-211`, `:220`).
- So `.nexus/.env` gets no line comparison, and a 4–16 MiB copy of a `.nexus` file passes. The comment says this is by design.
- `readFileSync` after `lstat` could block on a FIFO swapped in concurrently. This needs a live agent.
- A path staged-added and then deleted from disk is neither a source nor a deletion, so the comment at `:215` is slightly overstated. The content only ever existed in the index.

Contributing paths are named per row. Plain-only means the plain builder; main means `candidateDiff`.

| Way in | Caught? | Where / what remains |
|---|---|---|
| Protected source is a symlink (to a file, a directory, outside the repo, or dangling), a FIFO or socket, a directory in its place, over 4 MiB, or unreadable | Yes, both builders | `:206-224` set `complete = false`, so every new file is omitted. | New file is a symlink to a file or a dangling link | Shown as link text only | `:237`. Names the target, not content. |
| New file is a symlink to a directory | Plain only: leak or silent drop | F1. Main is fine. |
| Hardlink, either direction | Yes | A hardlink is a regular file, so it hits the hash or line match (`:241-242`). The test's "hardlink target" case uses an ignored `hard.txt`, so it exercises nothing extra. |
| Copy, partial copy, moved or renamed copy as a new file | Yes, if the source is still on disk | Hash and line match. A moved or deleted source is caught by `protectedChanged` (`:396` main, `:490` plain). |
| Partial copy with only short lines (under 8 characters) or `#` / `//` comment lines | No (residual) | A commented-out secret line such as `# KEY=sk-...` is not matched. |
| Reformatted copy (quoting, `export ` prefix, value only) | No (residual) | Exact trimmed-line match only. |
| Base64 or otherwise encoded copy | Out of scope | Redaction is the only guard. |
| Pasted lines in a modified tracked file | No (residual, documented) | Status M is never line-compared in either builder. Redaction is the only guard. |
| Tracked file replaced by a hardlink to `.env` | No (same residual) | Shows as M with the whole content. |
| Operator-only secrets in an isolated worktree | Yes | `protectedMatcher` `:422-433` lists the operator's `--cached`, `--others` and `--ignored` files under a pinned checkout. A listing failure propagates as an error, so it fails closed. Residual: non-UTF-8 names (F4), and untracked nested repositories in the operator checkout (directory entries are dropped at `:431`). |
| Tracked and deleted protected file | Yes for paths in the base | Both builders emit a D entry, which sets `protectedChanged`. |
| Intent-to-add entries | Yes | Main: `ownIndex` entries not in the base are intent-to-added, so they are sources. Plain: the private index lacks them, so they appear as untracked. |

| `security_reviewer` `unified_diff` | Main builder only | `operation_runner_execution.ts:698`, no plain fallback. Redacted afterwards. |
| Reviewer evidence | Main, or plain on an unsupported state | `:728-751`, redacted afterwards. |

## Ask 2: every skip in `protectedContent`, `protectedMatcher`, `carriedBy`

| Skip | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `:206-211` not a regular file and `structural` | Silent drop by design. It can drop a policy-protected `.nexus` link (F5). |
| `:206-211` not a regular file and not `structural` | Sets `complete = false`. |
| `:214-216` ENOENT | Silent. Safe for tracked files, since the caller flags deleted ones. Unsafe for U+FFFD names (F4). |
| `:214-216` other lstat errors | Sets `complete = false`. |
| `:220` `.nexus` file over 4 MiB | Silent drop by design (F5). |
| `:222`, `:224` oversized, total over 64 MiB, or read error | Sets `complete = false`. |
| `:226` structural: no lines taken | By design. |
| `carriedBy`: `!complete` | Returns true. |
| `carriedBy`: no sources at all | Returns false. Fine, no sources exist. |
| `carriedBy` catch (lstat or read error) | Returns true (omit). |
| `carriedBy` non-file and not a symlink | Returns true. |
| `carriedBy` symlink | Returns false: F1. |
| `carriedBy` over 16 MiB | Returns true. |
| `:418`, `:431` entries ending in `/` (nested repos) | Silent drop (residual). |
| Listing errors, timeouts, untrusted operator checkout | Propagate and fail closed. |

Callers use `carriedBy` only for A, C and R destinations in main (`:396`) and for untracked files in plain (`:493`). `complete = false` never changes how M entries are handled.

Yes. Both builders go through the same `protectedMatcher` and `protectedContent` functions. What differs is the source list (F3) and `protectedChanged`. A new protected untracked file sets `protectedChanged` in main (as an A group) but not in plain (`:490`). The protective effect is the same, because that file is itself a source.

## Ask 4: other non-regular skips in `specialist_inputs.ts` or `operation_git.ts`

- **`:142` (`snapshotSupport`)** and **`:262` (`attributesTree`)** skip a `.gitattributes` that is not a regular file. This hides no protected content. `check-attr` and the stripped attribute source remain the backstop.
- **`:344` (`onDisk`)** treats any lstat success as present. An intermediate symlink makes a later `git add` fail, which is a closed failure.
- **`operation_git.ts`** has no `lstat` or `isFile` in `snapshotCandidate`.
- **Carry-over:** the `carriedBy` symlink branch is the only non-regular skip that leaks (F1).

## Ask 5: staged-removal handling

Apart from F2, it behaves correctly:

- **Unmerged entries:** `diff-index` reports `U`, so they are not removed. The base entry is compared with the worktree, and a path not in the base shows as untracked. This is acceptable.
- **Intent-to-add:** I verified that `diff-index --cached` reports `M` for an intent-to-add over a path in the base, so the path is not removed. An intent-to-add path outside the base shows as untracked, which is fine.
- **Removed path that is also untracked and not ignored:** it is reported twice in plain, once as a deletion and once as a new file. It is counted twice toward the 2,000-path limit and twice in `omitted` if protected. Main shows only the deletion. This is an inconsistency, not a leak.
- **Skip-worktree and assume-unchanged flags:** `diff-index --cached` reads only entries and OIDs, so the flags do not matter. The private index has no flags.
- **Real index with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` unset under a pinned `--git-dir`:** `ownEnv` drops `GIT_*`, and the index resolves to `<git-dir>/index`, which is the admin directory for linked worktrees. This is correct. `diff-index --cached` does no content comparison, so no driver or filter can run.
- **Missing real index:** every base file would show as removed, which matches git's own view.
- **Trusted git:** every new git call goes through `git()`, which prepends `pin` (from `trustedGitArgs`) and `GIT_SAFE`. Confirmed: no call bypasses it. The operator listing is pinned via `verifyCheckout`.
- **Driver check:** it runs on the private index after removals, so removed paths are not driver-checked. That is harmless, because `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv` are set.

- **Security: true.** F1 and F3 are plausible exposures, and F4 is lower severity.

The "directory in its place" and "hardlink target" cases never reach the new branch, because the directory case yields a regular inner file and the hardlink is ignored. The "unreadable file" case passes trivially when run as root. There are no tests for a new symlink file, for a staged removal in a subdirectory, or for unchanged tracked protected files in plain.

In isolated worktrees the operator listing (`--cached`) covers this.

This over-omits whenever any protected symlink exists, which is the intended trade-off. |
| New file is a symlink to a file or a dangling link | Shown as link text only | `:237`. Names the target, not content. |
| New file is a symlink to a directory | Plain only: leak or silent drop | F1. Main is fine. |
| Hardlink, either direction | Yes | A hardlink is a regular file, so it hits the hash or line match (`:241-242`). The test's "hardlink target" case uses an ignored `hard.txt`, so it exercises nothing extra. |

| Partial copy with only short lines (under 8 characters) or `#` / `//` comment lines | No (residual) | A commented-out secret line such as `# KEY=sk-...` is not matched. |
| Reformatted copy (quoting, `export ` prefix, value only) | No (residual) | Exact trimmed-line match only. |
| Base64 or otherwise encoded copy | Out of scope | Redaction is the only guard. |
| Pasted lines in a modified tracked file | No (residual, documented) | Status M is never line-compared in either builder. Redaction is the only guard. |
| Tracked file replaced by a hardlink to `.env` | No (same residual) | Shows as M with the whole content. |
| Operator-only secrets in an isolated worktree | Yes | `protectedMatcher` `:422-433` lists the operator's `--cached`, `--others` and `--ignored` files under a pinned checkout. A listing failure propagates as an error, so it fails closed. Residual: non-UTF-8 names (F4), and untracked nested repositories in the operator checkout (directory entries are dropped at `:431`). |

| Intent-to-add entries | Yes | Main: `ownIndex` entries not in the base are intent-to-added, so they are sources. Plain: the private index lacks them, so they appear as untracked. |

## Ask 2: every skip in `protectedContent`, `protectedMatcher`, `carriedBy`

| Skip | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `:206-211` not a regular file and `structural` | Silent drop by design. It can drop a policy-protected `.nexus` link (F5). |
| `:206-211` not a regular file and not `structural` | Sets `complete = false`. |
| `:214-216` ENOENT | Silent. Safe for tracked files, since the caller flags deleted ones. Unsafe for U+FFFD names (F4). |
| `:214-216` other lstat errors | Sets `complete = false`. |
| `:220` `.nexus` file over 4 MiB | Silent drop by design (F5). |
| `:222`, `:224` oversized, total over 64 MiB, or read error | Sets `complete = false`. |
| `:226` structural: no lines taken | By design. |
| `carriedBy`: `!complete` | Returns true. |
| `carriedBy`: no sources at all | Returns false. Fine, no sources exist. |
| `carriedBy` catch (lstat or read error) | Returns true (omit). |
| `carriedBy` non-file and not a symlink | Returns true. |
| `carriedBy` symlink | Returns false: F1. |
| `carriedBy` over 16 MiB | Returns true. |

Callers use `carriedBy` only for A, C and R destinations in main (`:396`) and for untracked files in plain (`:493`). `complete = false` never changes how M entries are handled.

## Ask 3: is the `complete = false` rule applied equally?

Yes. Both builders go through the same `protectedMatcher` and `protectedContent` functions. What differs is the source list (F3) and `protectedChanged`. A new protected untracked file sets `protectedChanged` in main (as an A group) but not in plain (`:490`). The protective effect is the same, because that file is itself a source.

Apart from F2, it behaves correctly:

- **Supported domain.** `snapshotSupport` in `cli/src/core/specialist_inputs.ts` is a single predicate used by `candidateDiff` and the debugger snapshot. - **`operation_git.ts` git helpers.** Unpinned `gitResult` and `git` calls with a unit worktree as cwd exist there (the pre-existing issue you said is tracked separately).
- **Other blocking.** Non-predicate blockers on reviewers (path count over 2,000, driver refusal, timeouts) are unchanged, per your decision.

I fixed #434's blocking finding myself and committed it locally as `559d6982`, with a pre-push review running before it goes out.

- **The race:** after opening the file, the code now asks the kernel where the open descriptor really points, via `/proc/self/fd`. If it resolves outside the repo it is refused, and on Linux a failed lookup fails closed. That closes the parent-directory-swapped-for-a-symlink window the reviewer found.
- **Proof it works:** I caught that my first test mocked the wrong object and passed even with the check disabled, so I added an injectable `realpath` parameter to simulate the race deterministically. With the check disabled the suite fails (105 pass, 1 fail). With it enabled all 106 pass.
- **Other fixes:**
  - The FIFO assertion no longer sits inside a `catch` that swallows failures.
  - The ledger row states the Linux-only guarantee honestly.

The reviewer will check:
- That the check is correct when the repo root itself sits behind a symlinked path.
- That the file descriptor is closed on every path.
- That the new optional parameter can't be abused.
- That the non-Linux branch is documented honestly.

If it ACCEPTs I'll push and wait for Entire's re-review and CI. Meanwhile #469 is still on its last CI job, and #479's redactor fix is with its agent.

<result>### Starvation and monotonicity review of `00b9cd4a..HEAD` (`egress.ts`, `redactor_encoded_dotted.test.ts`)

**Verdict: 1 medium and 1 low-medium finding, both starvation shapes other than the documented one.** I ran every case below with throwaway `npx tsx` scripts in the scratchpad and wrote nothing into the repo. I did not run the repo's test suite.

### 1. Code Review

- **medium** `cli/src/core/egress.ts:~609` (`scanBase64Keys`, fresh-key charge): a run of accepted fresh keys exhausts the main budget at about half the text, so a later real key loses its dotted tail.
  - **Cause:** a fresh key with both an encoded and a dotted extension is charged twice for the same window. The loop `for (const end of new Set([runEnd, encodedEnd, extendedEnd]))` charges `encodedEnd-runEnd` and then `extendedEnd-runEnd`, so the charge is up to about 2x the window.
  - **Why the stated invariant fails:** the comment says fresh windows "cannot exceed the text", but charges can. The budget is `text.length + 1024`.
  - **Trigger:** space-separated units `REDACTED<3-char id>+%2F` + `a`×865 + `.Zk4Pq8R<i> `, repeated 20 times, then ` then REDACTED%2FJf5Ge0UaXo2RtBq.Mn5Qr7Vw2 end`.
  - **Result:** `redactDiagnosticForOutput` returns `then [REDACTED:OPENAI_API_KEY].Mn5Qr7Vw2 end`, so the tail leaks. Reproduced at a=865, 866 and 867. No exact filler length is required (see the next paragraph).
  - **Why it is easy to hit:** a rejected extension does not consume budget, so the leftover is just a modulus of the charges. The attacker adjusts the filler, or appends one small accepted unit, to drain the leftover to below the real key's extension. Other filler lengths leave a few hundred units of budget, which still starves any longer tail.
  - **Fix:** charge each fresh key once, for the largest accepted end only (`max` over the accepted ends, minus `runEnd`), or charge incrementally from the last charged end. I did not test this fix.
  - **Test gap:** "a blob of accepted encoded runs…" does not cover this. Its 14-character units overlap, so almost all of them are rescans, and none has a dotted tail. I have not run it against the old code.

- **low-medium** `egress.ts:~1145` (deterministic loop): starvation by overlapping windows in the shared `extensionBudget`.
  - **Cause:** every match draws on that budget, and the matches of a dot-joined blob have overlapping windows. For example, 30 × `ghp_<36>` joined by `.` makes each of about 25 matches charge roughly 1 KB against a budget of text+1024. The `sk-` scan's fresh/rescan split was not applied here, so the "own budget" does not help.
  - **Trigger:** 30 × `ghp_…` joined by `.`, then ` then <ghp_…>.Mn5Qr7Vw0.Mn5Qr7Vw1…Vw5 end`, a 54-character tail.
  - **Result:** `then [REDACTED:GITHUB_TOKEN].Mn5Qr7Vw0.Mn5Qr7Vw1.Mn5Qr7Vw2.Mn5Qr7Vw3.Mn5Qr7Vw4.Mn5Qr7Vw5 end`. The whole tail is in clear.
  - **Why it is worse than the first shape:** the real key here follows a space and is unrelated to the blob, so this is not the documented limitation. n=0 is covered, and n=30, 60, 100 and 200 all starve it.
  - **Not reproduced:** with a short 11-character tail on the `ghp` blob I could not make it starve, because tokens at the end of the blob have shorter windows and drain the leftover. The other prefixes (`AIza`, `hf_`, JWT) share this budget and code path, but I only ran the `hf_` variant, which also did not starve with a short tail.
  - **Fix:** use the same split as the `sk-` scan. Track `scannedTo` per pattern, charge the main budget only when `start >= scannedTo`, and charge overlapping matches to a small separate quota.
  - **Also:** `extensionBudget.left > 0` does not stop the scan once the leftover is small but non-zero. Each remaining match still scans up to 1024 characters and fails the charge. Throughput on a 3.3 MB dot-joined `ghp_` blob was about 0.7 µs per character, and 20k vs 80k tokens (4x text) took 610 ms vs 2249 ms. The cost is linear, with a constant of roughly 25x for tokens spaced about 41 characters apart. It is bounded by `MAX_EXTENSION` per match, but the "linear" claim hides that constant.

### 2. Security Review

- **Monotonicity: confirmed.**
  - **Mechanism:** in `scanBase64Keys`, the `runEnd` form is judged and pushed with no charge. `chargeExtension` runs only when `end > runEnd`, and failure only `continue`s past that longer end.
  - **Other paths:** the deterministic loop always pushes `ends[0]`. A rejected charge never removes the original match.
  - **Evidence:** the plain keys were still emitted in every starved run above, so no new plain-key leak was introduced. The leak is only the extension (the dotted or encoded tail, which is key material).
- **Linear cost in `scanBase64Keys`: confirmed.**
  - **Mechanism:** `from = max(runEnd, at+1)`, so runs are disjoint. Fresh windows are disjoint. Rescans are bounded by `rescanLeft = 16*len`, with every rescan costing at least 16.
  - **Residual:** a slice and a normalise per accepted end, which is 3x the run length at worst.
- **Other starvation shapes in the `sk-` scan:** I could not construct one besides finding 1.
  - **Separators:** windows stop at any non-key character (space, `"`, `=`, `:`), so a key after one is always fresh. `-`, `.`, `/` and `+` are key characters, so a key right after them is the documented "no separator" case.
  - **Nested `sk-`:** a nested `sk-` inside a run is skipped as before.
  - **Blob ends right before the key / last window spans the key:** both are the documented limitation, and the rescan quota is spent only by rescans.
  - **Rejected blobs** (`sk-%2F-`): they do not charge, as intended. The 280 KB test passes.

### 3. Slop: Low

The two strongest reasons are the weak test for the accepted-run case and unrelated scope.

- **Weak test (reason 1):** the "accepted encoded runs" test does not prove the new behaviour, as finding 1 shows. Each of its 14-character units sits inside the previous unit's 1 KB window, so only about 3 are fresh. It has no dotted tails, and its 180-character tail is the only thing it checks.
- **Unrelated scope (reason 2):** `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_view.rs` and the `README.md` worktree wording are unrelated to the redaction fix. The Rust test now hardcodes 11 and drops the check that the height follows `(rows + 5).clamp(8, 24)`. `docs/WORKTREES.md` exists, so the README link is fine.
- **Comment drift:** the `scanBase64Keys` comment ("windows are disjoint and so cannot exceed the text") is wrong because of the double charge. The `FINDINGS.md` entry claims the fix is complete, but the deterministic loop still starves.
- **Minor:** `chargeExtension` now returns a boolean while `newExtensionBudget` and `extendDottedKey` drop their parameters, which is clean. The `Set([runEnd, encodedEnd, extendedEnd])` plus per-end charge is what causes finding 1.

Probe scripts are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/6473a60e-9fa2-4bd9-9d0c-35324295cf68/scratchpad/` (`q2.ts`, `q3.ts`, `q6.ts`, `q8.ts`).</result>

Read-only review of `HEAD` against `origin/v1/v114-int-2`, `00b9cd4a` and `origin/main` 6e10ac9d. Nothing was executed, so the two findings below are traced from code, not run.

## (1) Monotonicity against origin/main: holds

**`sk-` scan.**
- The run is `scanKeyRun(at+3, false)`, the same character class as main's loop, including `\/`.
- `isBase64KeyRun(runEnd)` is main's predicate verbatim. The added `normalizeKeyChars` is a no-op on a run that has no `%` or look-alike characters, and a non-encoded run cannot contain them.
- `runEnd` is always the first member of the `Set`, so the original is emitted exactly as in main, including the `=` padding.
- `from = max(runEnd, at+1)` is unchanged, so the same candidates are visited. Extensions only add values.

**Pattern loop.**
- The original `end` is computed as in main and always emitted. The `>= 8` and `isReference` guards are unchanged.
- The extension is a second push that is never a replacement.
- The counter only gates the extra push.

**Entropy tokens.**
- Main required `/^[a-zA-Z0-9+/=_-]+$/` on `plain`, so any token with `%` or a look-alike never matched.
- The new `length` differs from `tok.length` only when a normalisation happened, and those tokens were never matched in main.
- Dotted tokens are new. Tokens with neither feature behave identically.

**Overlap resolution.**
- `resolveOverlaps` is untouched.
- A new longer same-start match cannot cause a drop that main did not have, because the drop rule needs the enclosing token's `end >= match.end`. I did not enumerate every `resolveOverlaps` interaction.

**`replaceValues`.** It changes versus main, but it is not in the loops you asked about. Its comment says the new union path only widens coverage.

## (2) Work and memory bound

**Work, constant extension cost: confirmed.**
- Every `scanKeyRun(..., true, ...)` and every `extendDottedKey` call sits behind `takeAttempt`.
- In `scanBase64Keys` the gate is `continues && takeAttempt`, and `encodedEnd` and `extendedEnd` both fall back to `runEnd` when `extend` is false.
- In the pattern loop it is `text[end]==='.' && takeAttempt`.
- `extendDottedKey`'s segments are disjoint inside one fixed `limit`, so one call scans at most about 2 × 1024 characters plus the failing segment.
- Total extension work is at most (1 + 7 families) × 1024 × about 3 × 1024 characters, independent of `n`.
- `matchEncodedKeyChar` is a sticky O(1) regex.
- Still linear in `n`: the regex scans, the original runs (disjoint because scanning resumes at `runEnd`), and `isBase64KeyRun` on the original run.

**Memory: the "constant" claim is wrong.**
- Each extended value is `text.slice(start, spanEnd)`, which contains the whole original run plus up to 1024 more characters.
- Runs are disjoint, so the sum is at most about 2n to 3n for the `sk-` family (`runEnd`, `encodedEnd` and `extendedEnd` are up to three separate strings). It is also at most n for each pattern family.
- Example: one 1 MB base64 run followed by `.Zk4Pq8Rt` yields about 2 MB of values, against 1 MB in main.
- The true bound is roughly (1 + c)·n + constant with c ≤ about 2 for `sk-` plus the pattern families, not a constant. The extension multiplies the replaced-value size, and with it the Aho-Corasick automaton size, by a constant factor.
- The test bound `input.length + EXTENSION_VALUE_ALLOWANCE` is additive and would not catch this. The constant's comment ("families x attempts x ~3 KB") also does not match the 4 MiB value: 8 × 1024 × 3 KB is about 24 MiB.

## (3) Starving a later real key

**Finding 1: cheap starvation of the `sk-` family, outside the documented limit.**
- The attempt is spent on any word-boundary `sk-` whose run is followed by `.` or an encoded character. There is no length or validity check, so these candidates are not "key-like". The counting site is `cli/src/core/egress.ts:598-600`.
- Trigger: `"sk-. ".repeat(1025)` (about 5 KB), or `"sk-%2F "` repeated, followed by `sk-<40 plain chars>%2F<more>.TAIL`.
- Effect: the original run `sk-<plain>` has no `/` or `+`, so `scanBase64Keys` rejects it. The bounded OPENAI pattern redacts the plain prefix, and everything after `%2F` stays in clear.
- The same trigger also loses the dotted tail of an `sk-` key found by `scanBase64Keys`.
- The `%2F` tail is handled only by the `sk-` family, so one cheap blob suffices. A dotted tail on a plain key needs the family that found it spent too: 1025 matching OPENAI keys followed by `.`, about 35 KB.
- This is the same class of leak as the finding being closed, only the threshold moved. Severity: Low. Confidence: 0.9, traced in code.
- Fix: take an attempt only when the run is long enough to be a key (body of at least 20 characters), or validate before spending, so the documented limit becomes true. Alternatively state the limit as "more than 1024 `sk-` + `.`/encoded occurrences". The existing "past 1024" test uses full-size candidates, so it does not cover this shape.

**Finding 2: attempts are consumed even when nothing continues.**
- In the pattern loop, `text[end]==='.'` is satisfied by any sentence-ending full stop after a key (`ghp_…xyz.`). The attempt is spent before `extendDottedKey` learns there is no continuation.
- This stays within the "key-like" limit, since the candidates are real regex matches. A log with more than 1024 real tokens, each followed by `.`, loses later dotted tails. It is a documentation point rather than a defect (Low, 0.8).

**Shapes checked that do not lose a tail within the limit.**
- Counters are per family, so one family cannot spend another's attempts. Cross-family starvation needs both families spent.
- Candidates that fall inside an earlier window are counted but cost no more than one attempt each.
- Accepted blobs and the `%2F` / `%252F` / look-alike unit shapes are counted the same way, one attempt per candidate. I found no way to spend more than one attempt per candidate.
- A key whose tail is longer than 1024 characters keeps only 1024 characters of it. This is a new, unstated per-candidate cap, and chained keys are unaffected because each key is its own candidate.
- Extensions are not followed after `=` padding (`…==.tail`), the same as in main.

## Entire-style reviews

**1. Code review.**
- Finding 1 above: Low, confidence 0.9.
- Finding 2 (counted without a continuation): Low, confidence 0.8, mostly a documentation point.
- The `sidecar.ts` change is correct. `withDurableSync<T>` returns the callback's value, the other callers of `saveSession` ignore the return, and the throw path sets `saved = false`.
- No other defects found.

**2. Security review.**
- Finding 1 is a partial-credential disclosure under attacker-influenced text. The attacker needs about 5 KB of crafted tool or file output ahead of a real encoded-tail key. The impact is the key's tail staying in clear.
- No new injection, authorisation or secrets-in-logs issues.

**3. Slop: Low to Medium. The two strongest reasons are:**
- The documentation overclaims. The `MAX_EXTENSION_ATTEMPTS_PER_FAMILY` comment and the FINDINGS.md row claim a constant value-memory bound and a "key-like" limit that the code does not enforce. The memory is linear with a multiplier (at most 2n to 3n for the `sk-` family), and the counted candidates are any `sk-.` or `sk-%2F`.
- The `EXTENSION_VALUE_ALLOWANCE` comment contradicts its value, and the test bound is additive only. It cannot detect the multiplicative growth from long original runs.

- The `ExtensionAttempts` / `newExtensionAttempts` / `takeAttempt` trio is heavy for a number you decrement (`left` is a counter and nothing more).

- **Trigger:** about 40 KB of dense dotted keys per family (`ghp_<36>.Zk4Pq8x001.Zk4Pq8x002...`, one such chain per family) feeds all 8 families. That is a text of about 300-400 KB. **2. Medium (test), `cli/test/redactor_encoded_dotted.test.ts` (`EXTENSION_VALUE_ALLOWANCE = 32 * 1024 * 1024`, and the 20 s bounds)**

- The 20 s wall-clock bound would pass a 4x regression.

With ANY counter, a blob of cheap `sk-%2F-` (or `sk-.`) look-alikes spends it and a later real key keeps only its plain prefix (its dotted/encoded tail stays in clear): this is Entire's original Low 01M76CJKRA0T. Windows of one family are therefore disjoint by construction: total extension work per family is O(n), values total <= ~3n (each extended value repeats its run once; windows disjoint), and NOTHING earlier in the text can spend what a later key needs (no shared pool, no counter, no rescan accounting, no budget objects). A candidate immediately followed by another candidate simply does not extend into it (the next candidate extends itself, and the union of redactions covers both). Keep: the original match ALWAYS emitted (monotone vs origin/main b696c3d2 / the pre-extension behaviour); the existing extension semantics inside a window (extendDottedKey/encoded handling, isKeyMaterialSegment, isBase64KeyRun); `from = Math.max(runEnd, at+1)` progress rule in the sk- scanner. DELETE: MAX_EXTENSION_ATTEMPTS_PER_FAMILY, ExtensionAttempts, takeAttempt, newExtensionAttempts and every use. Keep MAX_EXTENSION=1024 as the window cap. Cross-family overlap is allowed (each family partitions its own windows) so total work <= (number of families) x n x constant; state that bound in ONE comment sentence. HONEST LIMIT to write in the code comment and in docs/v1.1.4/FINDINGS.md (row for 01M76CJKRA0T; replace the old text, which mentions 1024/128 candidates): 'a key's extension stops at the next candidate of the same family or after 1024 characters; the original match is never dropped. A real key whose own tail contains another candidate start (e.g. `sk-` inside the tail) is covered by that candidate's own window.' and nothing about counters or starvation by count. Also state total work/size bound truthfully (families x O(n); values <= ~3n + per-family constant).
